items.title: Northrop Grumman To Boost Missile Component Production For ‘Arsenal of Freedom’ – Retail Views Steady Execution To Be Key For Growth
items.summary: The company, among other things, is doubling capacity at its Utah facilities to deliver solid rocket motors and nearly tripling capacity at the Allegany Ballistics Lab in West Virginia.

items.title: The Production Ramp That Could Repower Boeing Stock
items.summary: Boeing is delivering airplanes at a pace it has not managed in years, and almost none of the profit those airplanes will carry has shown up yet.

items.title: Northrop Grumman Enters $3 Billion Contracts to Increase Missile Defense Production
items.summary: Northrop Grumman signed two agreements totaling $3 billion to speed up production of missile interceptors.

items.title: Russian barrage kills nine in Kyiv, damages Lithuanian embassy
items.summary: Investing.com -- Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight, killing nine people, injuring at least 30 and damaging Lithuania’s embassy, Ukrainian and Lithuanian officials said on Saturday.

items.title: U.S. and allies display growing naval cooperation in Pacific drills
items.summary: Investing.com -- The U.S. and its allies conducted their largest Rim of the Pacific maritime exercise to date, demonstrating deepening military cooperation amid concerns about China and North Korea, the Wall Street Journal reported.

items.title: GE vs. Northrop: Which Aerospace & Defense Stock Should You Bet On?
items.summary: GE Aerospace tops NOC on stronger growth estimates, share gains and commercial engine momentum despite a steeper valuation.

items.title: The U.S. Just Took A Big Step to Break China's Magnet Dominance
items.summary: The push to end China's dominance in rare earth magnets is gaining momentum as North America builds an integrated supply chain from mine to magnet.

items.title: L3Harris Missile Business Is Booming. So Why Is the Stock Tanking?
items.summary: The defense contractor reported second-quarter earnings per share of $3.13. Wall Street was looking for $2.80.
